doc.title: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey Interview, 1959-03-15
doc.interviewee: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey

title: Amos Riley, Alex Scott, the Nola band and other names
summary: As the visit ends they list Amos Riley, Alex Scott, Eddie Jackson and the Nola band and other musicians.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, we must run along in a couple of minutes.
Well, you got Amos Roddy, I know you. Yes, we had a nice... And uh... Alex Scott. Amos Roddy.
Wait, we didn't see Amos Roddy. Amos Roddy. He was a trumpet player.
Yeah, trumpet player. He had the two-lane band, the brass band. All the dog fellas. And his nephew, Alex Scott. He was a very good bass player. Very good. Very good.
Alex used to play with me. Alex used to play with me.
I knew you didn't talk about Jimmy Pauline. Oh, yes. Yes. And Spencer. Wow.
David used to play with Tronman. Yeah. Nox at Butts.
Well, that's a hit of mine. I know nothing about him. John McCullough at the Browns, you should know. Yeah, I don't remember. Are you supposed to play with Tronman?
Yeah. I don't remember. Are you supposed to play with him?
Yeah, I don't remember. Are you supposed to play with him?
New York, how are you supposed to play with Tronman?
Mm-hmm. I used to play with Tronman.

Oh, yeah. Eddie Jackson. I played with his band, too. The Nola band. The Nola band. Yeah. The Nola band. I played with the Nola band. You remember that. You played. You played with the band. Yeah. Eddie Jackson, Peter La Caz. And who had, I don't know what was it, Paul's band? Or, what? Heisenbaum. Heisenbaum.

Heisenbaum. Heisenbaum. Oh, we had a whole lot of musicians around there. Oh, yeah. There were so many. Yeah, you'd remember. You'd be writing a long time. Every once in a while, I'd think about some new ones.
